title: NDFI-to-regulated-bank contagion via collateral fraud - the Zions / Western Alliance / Cantor Group episode (Oct 2025)
source: Public record (Oct 2025): SEC filings + reporting (Bloomberg, Reuters, CNBC, WSJ). Zions Bancorporation disclosed 'apparent misrepresentations and contractual defaults' on two related commercial-and-industrial loans totaling ~$60M from its California Bank & Trust division, taking a provision for the full amount and charging off ~$50M in Q3 2025; Zions sued to recover >$60M lent to investment funds Cantor II and Cantor IV, which had drawn revolving credit facilities to buy DISTRESSED commercial-mortgage loans. The next day Western Alliance disclosed it had sued the same borrower group - entities managed by the same leadership, incl. Cantor Group V - alleging forged title-insurance documents concealing overlapping liens, seeking ~$100M. Market reaction: Zions ~-12%, Western Alliance ~-11%, the KBW Nasdaq Regional Banking Index ~-4%, spillover to Great Southern / Customers Bancorp / Hingham; comparisons to the 2023 SVB/First Republic churn. Context: JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon had days earlier cited the Tricolor (subprime auto) and First Brands (auto parts) bankruptcies - 'when you see one cockroach, there's probably more.' IMPORTANT DISAMBIGUATION: this 'Cantor Group' is a commercial-real-estate fund group - NOT Cantor Fitzgerald (the Lutnick firm); they are unrelated. HONESTY/GRADE: the filings, charge-off, lawsuits, share moves, and index move are FACT; the allegations are ALLEGATIONS (litigation pending, borrowers not adjudicated); analysts split - some called it idiosyncratic/isolated (Zions said total criticized assets were LOWER than Jun 30 2025; Western Alliance affirmed guidance), others saw it as an early NDFI-contagion signal - BOTH views recorded. This is the concrete, named case of the exact channel the corpus tracks abstractly (private-credit/NDFI stress reaching REGULATED banks); it is the Oct 2025 precedent, carried as documented history, not as breaking news. Overlay + the two real loan edges only; dollar figures in notes/amounts; the AI-financial SCC is untouched (these nodes are isolated from the AI-compute core).

edges.note: Zions lent ~$60M via two related C&I revolvers (Cantor II / Cantor IV) from California Bank & Trust; took a full provision and charged off ~$50M in Q3 2025 after finding apparent misrepresentations + collateral subordination; sued to recover >$60M (fact of the loan + charge-off; the fraud is an allegation, litigation pending).

Western Alliance lent ~$100M to Cantor Group V (same leadership); sued alleging forged title-insurance documents concealing overlapping liens. WAL affirmed guidance, framing it as contained (fact of the loan + suit; fraud alleged, not adjudicated).

The Cantor funds drew the bank revolvers to buy DISTRESSED commercial-mortgage loans - so bank credit flowed through an NDFI into distressed CRE, the leg that links regulated-bank balance sheets to the CRE downturn (fact of the use-of-proceeds).

The Cantor funds sit in the NON-DEPOSITORY FINANCIAL INSTITUTION (NDFI) bucket - bank lending to NDFIs is the specific contagion channel investors zeroed in on (cross-ref macro-private-credit-bdc-stress, macro-uncovered-risk-pools). The episode made NDFI exposure the post-Oct-2025 regional-bank watch item (fact of the channel; contagion severity = labeled interpretation).
Same NDFI-lending channel: a regulated regional bank extending revolvers to a non-bank fund that then takes the underlying credit/collateral risk (fact of the channel).

Framing: days earlier Jamie Dimon cited the Tricolor (subprime auto) and First Brands (auto parts) bankruptcies - 'when you see one cockroach, there's probably more' - setting the credit-anxiety backdrop against which the Zions/WAL disclosures were read (fact of the statement; the systemic read is labeled).
The distressed loans the funds bought are commercial mortgages - tying the episode to the broader CRE/mortgage stress thread (fact).
